Galaxy Research: Crypto VC Funding Rebounds to $5.6 Billion in Q2, Up 31% QoQ

Galaxy Research reported that crypto and blockchain venture funding rebounded in Q2 2026 after cooling in the first quarter. VCs invested about $5.6 billion across 384 deals, with capital deployed up 31% quarter-over-quarter and deal count up 10%, driven mainly by later-stage financings. At the first-half pace, full-year 2026 investment would reach about $20.04 billion, slightly below 2025 but above most of 2023 and 2024.

Fed Raises Rates by 25 Bps to 3.75%–4.00%; 16 of 18 Officials See at Least One More Hike in 2026

Just In: The Federal Reserve’s FOMC voted unanimously, 12–0, to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00%, while continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system. The FOMC said the U.S. economy continues to expand at a solid pace, domestic spending remains resilient, productivity growth and capital investment are strong, and the labor market is broadly stable. Uncertainty remains elevated, in part due to geopolitical developments.

Celsius’ bankruptcy estate sued entities linked to BitMEX in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York on Sept. 12. The complaint alleges fraud, market manipulation and wrongful liquidations during Bitcoin’s March 2020 crash, involving 6,360 BTC worth approximately $495 million at the time of filing.

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig: Agency Will Advance Crypto Rules Under Existing Statutory Authority

U.S. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said on X that yesterday’s Senate vote was unfortunate and that Americans deserve regulatory clarity, legal certainty and consumer protections in crypto asset markets. He said President Trump had promised to deliver a future-proof crypto asset regulatory market structure, adding that the CFTC would help advance it using its existing statutory authority. Selig added that the CFTC is ready to issue rules for the “new frontier of finance.” — link

U.S. House to Consider Crypto Tax and Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bills Today

According to Eleanor Terrett, although the Clarity Act may be stalled in the Senate, the House will continue considering crypto-related legislation today. At 10:00 a.m. ET, the House Ways and Means Committee will mark up a crypto tax bill, while the House Financial Services Committee will begin considering several bills, including the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve bill introduced by Rep. Nick Begich earlier this year. — link

Circle Launches Arc Mainnet with BlackRock and Visa as Validators, Mints 10 Billion ARC Tokens

Circle has launched the public mainnet of Arc, an open Layer 1 blockchain for financial markets and agentic activity.

More than 100 applications and 100+ institutions and ecosystem builders are live at launch. Founding validators include BlackRock, DTCC, Galaxy, ICE, Mastercard, SBI Group, Standard Chartered and Visa.

Arc uses USDC for gas and offers sub-second finality. Circle also completed the genesis mint of 10 billion ARC tokens but said this does not commit it to a public token launch. — lin

Bernstein: SEC and CFTC May Accelerate Rulemaking After CLARITY Act Stalls

Bernstein analysts expect the SEC and CFTC to accelerate rules on token taxonomy, DeFi and self-custody protections, equity tokenization, real-world asset perpetual futures and sports event contracts. They said a CLARITY Act re-vote is unlikely due to limited time and concerns over its ethics provisions. — link

Kraken Parent Payward Plans to Offer Onchain Perpetual Futures to U.S. Clients, Starting with Hyperliquid

Payward, Kraken’s parent company, plans to offer onchain perpetual futures to U.S. clients, starting with Hyperliquid’s HIP-3 markets, subject to regulatory approval.

The markets would run on Hyperliquid’s public blockchain, with Payward’s CFTC-regulated Bitnomial handling deployment, clearing and settlement. NinjaTrader Clearing would carry client accounts, and trading would be limited to users approved and whitelisted by both entities. — link

Germany's Largest Bank to Launch Crypto Custody Services

According to Bloomberg, Germany's largest lender, Deutsche Bank AG, has announced plans to launch an institutional-grade cryptocurrency custody service, marking its formal entry into digital asset storage. Pending regulatory approvals, the bank expects to roll out the service later this year, enabling institutional and corporate clients to securely hold and transfer Bitcoin, Ethereum, and select stablecoins, with future roadmaps expanding into tokenized financial instruments. — link

Spot Bitcoin ETFs Saw Total Net Outflows of $450 Million on September 15

According to SoSoValue data, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw total net outflows of $450 million on September 15 Eastern Time, led by Fidelity's FBTC with a net outflow of $215 million. Meanwhile, spot Ethereum ETFs recorded total net outflows of $141 million, led by BlackRock's ETHA with $97.9738 million in net outflows. — link

UK FCA Releases Cryptoasset Regulatory Guidance, Authorization Applications to Open on Sept. 30

The UK’s FCA has released guidance on the scope of the country’s future cryptoasset regime. 

The regime will take effect on Oct. 25, 2027, with authorization applications opening on Sept. 30, 2026. The guidance covers qualifying stablecoin issuance, crypto trading platforms, dealing and arranging, custody, and staking services.

The FCA will consult on targeted updates in October following recent legislative changes. — link
